newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rosneft signs for extra Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rosneft signs for extra Iraqi oil.

text.p: Russian state oil holding company Rosneft has signed a deal to purchase an additional one million tonnes (7.4 million barrels) of Iraqi oil under the U.N. oil-for-food-deal, a senior industry official said on Friday.

Yuri Agababov, deputy director of Zarubezhneft, which is coordinating all Russian purchases of Iraqi oil, could not say over what period of time the volume would be lifted, but Interfax news agency said it would take place in April.
Interfax said Rosneft had begun lifting some of its earlier contracted volumes, which total 400,000 tonnes (2.96 million barrels), from Mina al-Bakr on Wednesday.
Rosneft's new contract for 7.4 million barrels brings Russian companies' total Iraqi oil entitlement to 32.6 million barrels over a six month period from December 1996.

Interfax said Rosneft's new volumes would be lifted from the Turkish port of Ceyhan and sent to Bulgaria's Bourgas refinery. The latter is run by Rosbulneft, a joint venture between Rosneft and Bulgaria's Neftochim.
Agababov could not immediately confirm how much oil the seven Russian companies holding Iraqi crude contracts had lifted so far.

Iraq began exporting oil last December for the first time in six years under a deal with the United Nations which allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of crude over six months to buy food and medicine.
